title: ButtonGroup.select() fails when options use format_func or are not primitive strings
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

ButtonGroup.select(...) in streamlit.testing.v1 crashes with a TypeError when used with option objects (not plain strings),  This makes it impossible to programmatically select a button in tests unless the value is a raw string.

Code below fails with `TypeError: 'in <string>' requires string as left operand, not Option`


### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st
options = ['List', 'Create', 'Update']
st.segmented_control(
            label="Section",
            options=options,
            selection_mode="single",
            default=options[0],
        )
#---- in test with pytest
from streamlit.testing.v1 import AppTest

def test_button_group_selection():
    at = AppTest.from_file("app.py").run()
    at.button_group[0].select("List").run()  # or even
```

### Steps To Reproduce

_No response_

### Expected Behavior

Calling .select() with an actual entry from .options should work regardless of how options are displayed (with or without format_func). At least, passing a value that already exists in .value should not break.

### Current Behavior

TypeError: 'in <string>' requires string as left operand, not Option

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.45.1
- Python version: 3.12
- Operating System: macOS 15.5
- Browser:  testing mode


### Additional Information

_No response_

We're aware of gaps in our AppTest functionality, and unfortunately, there's no immediate timeline for a resolution. We'll leave this issue open so we can gauge interest and better prioritize when to address it. Thanks for your understanding.

Hi! Triaging older AppTest bugs this week — I think this one has shipped and can be closed.

The `'in <string>' requires string as left operand, not Option` error came from the AppTest `ButtonGroup` wrapper round-tripping the proto's option payload (a `ButtonGroupProto.Option` message) through string-typed code. That serialization was reworked in [#13838](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/13838) ("Fix `pills` and `segmented_control` `format_func` regression in AppTest", commit `659b040b1`).

On current `develop`, options are stored as their formatted string content — see [`lib/streamlit/testing/v1/element_tree.py:733-734`](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/develop/lib/streamlit/testing/v1/element_tree.py#L733-L734):
```python
# Store formatted content strings for value serialization
self.options = [opt.content for opt in proto.options]
```
and `formatted_values` / `indices` consume those strings, so the `Option`-vs-string mismatch the original report describes can't occur anymore. The PR explicitly notes "Tested both single-select and multi-select modes [...] with custom format functions."

If you can re-run your failing test against a Streamlit version that includes #13838 (1.51.x line and later) and still hit a `TypeError` from `.select(...)`, please share the new traceback — happy to dig further if a different code path is still broken. Otherwise this should be safe to close.

(Disclosure: I drafted this comment with help from Claude Code while triaging stale issues; the references above were verified manually against the current `develop` branch.)
Thank you for the nudge here [USER]. It does look like this has been fixed, closing this as completed.
